accident_report:
(1) Vehicle initialization

On a straight, level, one-way roadway with four lanes and a wide right shoulder, three vehicles are traveling in the same direction under severe weather with continuous heavy rain. The pavement is wet, tire-road friction is reduced, and visibility is shortened, but all vehicles are still moving within a stable traffic flow. V1 is in lane 2, slightly ahead of the other vehicles, traveling at 72 km/h in a steady cruising state. Its driver intends to continue straight while maintaining a conservative following gap to the vehicle ahead. V2 is in lane 3, about 18 meters behind the rear of V1, traveling at 96 km/h. It is closing on slower traffic and intends to continue forward while searching for a faster path through the flow. V3 is in lane 1, about 10 meters behind the front of V1 and slightly to V1’s right rear, traveling at 68 km/h. It is moving steadily and intends to continue straight in lane 1. In front of V3, still in lane 1, V4 is traveling at 62 km/h and maintaining a safe following distance from traffic farther ahead. Its driver intends to remain in lane 1 because of the open wide shoulder on the right and the generally slower flow in that lane.

(2) Scene development

As the rain continues, the wet road surface lengthens braking distance for all vehicles and makes lateral tire grip weaker than under dry conditions. V2, traveling 24 km/h faster than V1, approaches from lane 3 with a large speed difference. Because V2 closes the gap rapidly in the reduced-visibility weather, its driver judges that staying in lane 3 will require a stronger deceleration than desired. Instead of waiting, V2 makes an illegal cut-in from lane 3 into lane 2, entering the gap directly ahead of V1 with only about 8 meters of longitudinal clearance.

This maneuver immediately changes V1’s state. Although V1 had been following safely before the cut-in, the inserted gap is now far below what is appropriate for 72 km/h on a wet surface. V1 responds with firm braking to avoid striking V2 from behind, reducing speed from 72 km/h to 54 km/h over a short distance. Because the road is wet and the weather is poor, V1’s deceleration is effective but not sharp enough to instantly rebuild a safe gap.

V2’s illegal cut-in also affects V3. After entering lane 2, V2 encounters slower traffic ahead than expected and cannot continue at 96 km/h. The driver brakes, dropping to 70 km/h. This causes V1 to remain under braking pressure behind V2. At the same time, V1’s speed reduction makes V3’s driver perceive lane 2 as temporarily slower than lane 1. However, V3 is now approaching V4 in lane 1, because V4 is traveling at only 62 km/h. To avoid closing too much on V4, V3 eases off the accelerator and lightly brakes to 60 km/h, which in turn compresses the spacing between V3 and V4.

A few seconds later, V2 tries to recover progress by moving right again. Seeing the wide shoulder beside lane 1, the driver of V2 misjudges the usable lateral space and attempts another aggressive merge, this time from lane 2 toward lane 1, aiming to pass the slower lane-2 flow. Because of the heavy rain, the wet pavement, and the reduced lateral grip, V2 cannot place the vehicle smoothly. V2 cuts into lane 1 ahead of V3 with insufficient clearance, forcing V3 to brake harder from 60 km/h to 42 km/h. This stronger braking by V3 immediately affects V4 ahead: V4’s driver notices that V3 is no longer maintaining its prior stable spacing and responds by braking from 62 km/h to 48 km/h to preserve distance to traffic ahead and avoid being overtaken into conflict space.

The interaction chain now tightens across all four vehicles. V2 is unstable in lane 1 because the illegal merge was initiated with excessive relative speed and on a wet surface. Its rear tires experience reduced grip during the lateral correction, and the vehicle drifts slightly left within lane 1. V3, already braking behind V2, cannot move to lane 2 because V1 is still there, offset to V3’s left front and also constrained by V2’s earlier maneuver. V4, after braking in front of V3, leaves V3 with less forward escape space than before. The severe weather, wet road, and repeated large speed adjustments have now linked all vehicles into a tightly constrained situation.

(3) Result

The scene ends at the first vehicle-to-vehicle collision. As V2 continues correcting its path on the wet roadway after the second illegal cut-in, it loses further longitudinal stability and slows more than V3 can comfortably accommodate in the compressed gap. V3, already forced down to 42 km/h and with V4 occupying the space ahead, cannot avoid impact. The front of V3 collides with the rear of V2 in lane 1. This is the first collision in the scenario, and it is the direct result of the combined effects of severe weather, wet pavement, a large speed difference, and V2’s repeated illegal cut-in maneuvers disrupting previously safe car-following conditions.

Initial actions: 
(V1): V1 drives on Lane 2 at 72 km/h maintaining a conservative following gap; (V2): V2 drives on Lane 3 at 96 km/h closing on slower traffic; (V3): V3 drives on Lane 1 at 68 km/h moving steadily; (V4): V4 drives on Lane 1 at 62 km/h maintaining a safe following distance.


Interactive pattern sequence: 
(V1, V2): V2 accelerates and swerves right to cut into the lane ahead of V1; (V1, V2): V1 brakes as V2 cuts into its lane, and V2 decelerates after the cut-in; (V2, V3): V2 decelerates and swerves right to cut into the lane ahead of V3, and V3 brakes to avoid collision; (V3, V4): V3 brakes and V4 decelerates in response to V3’s braking.
